source.title: The Slingshot Effect: A Late-Stage Optimization Anomaly in Adaptive Gradient Methods
source.authors: Vimal Thilak; Etai Littwin; Shuang-Fei Zhai; O. Saremi; Roni Paiss; Josh M. Susskind

record.file_problem: Full paper and appendix text supplied.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether late-stage Adam-family training behavior tracks held-out performance using grokking, vision and synthetic-data setups, rather than testing memorization of random labels or the original versions' interventions.
record.gate_note: Reports held-out accuracy/loss changes around Slingshot events and with optimizer settings, regularization, and normalization. Rows omit cited results and figure-only comparisons without sufficient textual outcome descriptions; rows capture reported aggregate statements where the text does not give individual values.
record.test_reason: The study measures Slingshot dynamics and delayed generalization, which none of V1–V8 names. Its Adam–SGD comparison uses modular arithmetic rather than V4's image-classification or language benchmarks. Its curvature measures do not test V7's magnitude-aware perturbation measure or ranking of generalization gaps.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate: the authors identify cyclic late-stage instability in Adam-family optimization, associate it with grokking and often improved generalization, and lack a satisfactory theoretical explanation. Qualify the norm-control account: Appendix C.1 reports that weight decay retains instability, while normalization stabilizes selected division and multiplication settings but can retain late instability on subtraction.
record.recipe_differences: Studies late-stage optimization instability and its association with held-out performance, mainly on algorithmic datasets and CIFAR-10; it does not test arbitrary-label memorization or the claim versions' specified comparisons.
record.method_sensitivity: Adam epsilon changes Slingshot and generalization outcomes; learning rate and training sample count condition the ViT CIFAR-10 results; weight decay and normalization temperature change stability and validation performance; SGD versus Adam-family optimizer changes the observed Slingshot/generalization pattern.

fits_no_version.finding: Slingshot cycles often coincide with delayed held-out improvements, although some CIFAR-10 configurations achieve their best accuracy before Slingshot. Epsilon strongly affects these outcomes.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Late-stage Adam instability is associated with improved generalization in some settings, with dependence on optimizer hyperparameters and dataset.

fits_no_version.finding: Weight decay can produce high validation accuracy quickly without Slingshot, while appropriately tuned feature and classifier normalization can preserve high accuracy with stable training.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Explicit norm control can provide alternatives to Slingshot-associated generalization; stability depends on the intervention and setting.

fits_no_version.finding: Momentum SGD shows no generalization on modular division across three learning rates despite receiving three times Adam's update budget.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adam can generalize where momentum SGD fails in the tested modular-division Transformer setup.

record.problems: Many outcomes are described qualitatively or presented only in plots; numerical test/validation values and uncertainty estimates are generally absent. Some settings use small training subsets. The paper states that it lacks a satisfactory theoretical explanation.
record.rows_left_out: Figure-only traces across many individual datasets, optimizer settings, and epsilon/beta sweeps were not separately extracted where the text did not give a condition-specific held-out outcome; see Figures 2–5, 13–21, 22–50. Figure 51–54 mode-connectivity analysis was not extracted because it reports interpolation loss barriers, not a versioned claim measure.

untested.parts: Matched random-label fitting and natural-label generalization, including chance-level random-label test accuracy.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected held-out performance and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD held-out performance on image-classification or language benchmarks under limited or broader tuning, including recovery interventions.
Large versus small batches under fixed epoch budgets and recipe changes that reduce the penalty.
Dropout versus no-dropout held-out error and its dependence on data size, dropout strength and augmentation.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance ranking generalization gaps against norm- and margin-based measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: All row states are cannot_determine relative to V1–V8 because their measures and comparisons do not establish those versions' effects. This does not negate the reported Slingshot or generalization findings. Training-time double descent is not V2's width-dependent claim, and update-direction curvature is not V7's magnitude-aware sharpness measure.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Adaptive optimizer versus SGD held-out performance under matched tuning.
Large versus small batch held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets.
Magnitude-aware sharpness ranking of generalization gaps.
Removing memorized examples and measuring test accuracy.

rows.subject: 2-layer decoder-only Transformer, width 128, 4 attention heads, approximately 450K trainable parameters
rows.operation_detail: Trained with Adam on modular division; validation accuracy rises during late-stage training around Slingshot cycles.

conditions.value: modular division, training and validation split
Adam; learning rate 0.001; weight decay 0; β1 = 0.9, β2 = 0.98, ϵ = 10−8

rows.baseline: Validation accuracy does not change until much later in training
rows.value: validation accuracy starts improving after 105 steps
rows.note: Grokking-style delayed validation improvement; no exact endpoint accuracy stated.
rows.check: The delayed improvement begins after 10^5 steps, approximately 100,000, not 105 steps; superscript formatting was lost. Delayed generalization alone tests no version.

rows.subject: 2-layer decoder-only Transformer, width 128, 4 attention heads, approximately 450K trainable parameters
rows.operation_detail: Compared Adam epsilon values on modular division, retaining the other setup.
rows.value: shows no sign of generalization even after receiving 500K updates
rows.note: The text explicitly reports no generalization for the largest tested epsilon.
rows.check: The reported lack of generalization at epsilon 10^-5 concerns grokking, not an effect named by any version.

rows.subject: Transformer
rows.operation_detail: Trained on subsets of CIFAR-10 with Adam; best test accuracy compared before and after first Slingshot.
rows.measure: Highest test accuracy for a set of hyperparameters
rows.baseline: pre-Slingshot checkpoints sometimes have better test accuracy
rows.value: Best test accuracy is typically achieved after Slingshot begins; some hyperparameter combinations are better before the first Slingshot
rows.note: Mixed result across hyperparameter combinations; no separate numerical values are given in the text.
rows.check: Checkpoint timing relative to Slingshot tests no version. The baseline field describes an exception to the aggregate result rather than a distinct baseline measurement.

rows.subject: 3-layer MLP with ReLU activations
rows.operation_detail: Trained on subset parity with Adam at ϵ = 10−8; test accuracy improves around most Slingshot events.

conditions.value: (n, k) subset parity; k = 3, n = 50; 1000 training samples, test set of 8000 samples

rows.value: a bump in generalization post most Slingshots
rows.note: Text describes a qualitative improvement; no exact accuracy values are reported there.
rows.check: Test-accuracy improvements around Slingshots on subset parity test no version.

rows.subject: 3-layer MLP with ReLU activations
rows.operation_detail: Compared Adam epsilon values on subset parity; higher epsilon yielded no Slingshots and generalization remained poor.
rows.baseline: ϵ = 10−8 runs show test-accuracy improvement around most Slingshots
rows.value: for larger values of ϵ, no Slingshots are observed, while generalization remains poor
rows.note: Explicit negative result for generalization in the higher-epsilon conditions.
rows.check: Poor generalization under higher Adam epsilon on subset parity tests no version; it is not evidence that a version's effect is absent.

rows.subject: Vision Transformer
rows.operation_detail: Trained with Adam on full CIFAR-10; test accuracy observed around Slingshot events.
rows.value: test accuracy peaks in epochs following a Slingshot; maximum recorded test accuracy occurs very late in optimization
rows.note: Qualitative result; no exact peak accuracy in the text.
rows.check: Late test-accuracy peaks under Adam provide no optimizer, width, architecture, batch-size, dropout, sharpness-ranking or example-removal comparison required by the versions.

rows.subject: 4-layer fully-connected network (FCN)
rows.operation_detail: Trained with Adam on synthetic data; best validation accuracy occurs late and in a Slingshot run across epsilon settings.

conditions.value: synthetic 128-dimensional dataset with 3 informative dimensions and 8 classes; 256 training and validation samples

rows.value: Adam reaches its best test accuracy late in optimization with ϵ = 10−5 yielding the highest validation accuracy; the best accuracy is achieved with a model that experiences Slingshot
rows.note: The figure caption and prose say validation accuracy; prose also calls it test accuracy.
rows.check: The maximum validation accuracy selected over checkpoints and epsilon settings is a synthetic-data result outside the versions. Preserve its status as a selected maximum rather than a fixed-checkpoint outcome.

rows.subject: Transformer
rows.operation_detail: AdamW weight decay on division data; increasing weight decay removes Slingshot and grokking while validation accuracy becomes high quickly.
rows.baseline: unregularized model generalizes later with Slingshot
rows.value: as weight decay strength increases, both Slingshot Effects and Grokking disappear with the model reaching high validation accuracy quickly
rows.note: Text states a qualitative outcome across the weight-decay sweep.
rows.check: Weight decay improving modular-division generalization does not test V4's recovery of an adaptive-versus-SGD deficit or V6's dropout comparison. Appendix C.1 explicitly reports remaining training instability despite removing Slingshot cycles.

rows.subject: Transformer
rows.operation_detail: Feature and parameter normalization with temperature on division data stabilizes training and preserves high validation accuracy at a selected temperature.
rows.baseline: lower temperatures show training instability; no numeric baseline stated
rows.value: temperature = 0.25 results in Grokking as validation accuracy improves late in training and high validation accuracy without training instability
rows.note: Selected normalization condition; not a test of dropout or the versions' mapped regularization claim.
rows.check: Feature and classifier normalization at a selected temperature tests no version. The stable, high-validation-accuracy result is supported for division at temperature 0.25.

rows.subject: Transformer
rows.operation_detail: SGD with momentum on modular division; no Slingshot, grokking or generalization observed.
rows.baseline: Adam showed Slingshot and generalization in the reported setup
rows.value: no evidence of Slingshot; no evidence of Grokking or generalization
rows.note: Authors ran three learning rates; the stated result is aggregate.
rows.check: The SGD result is supported for modular division, with three learning rates and 1.5 million steps. This algorithmic task falls outside V4's image-classification and language benchmark scope.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
